text:
Recent work supports changing the learning signal, with caution around aggressive hardness. [Sampled softmax (TOIS 2024)](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf) analyzes informative hard-negative gradients and ranking benefits; [PSL (NeurIPS 2024)](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/db1d5c63576587fc1d40d33a75190c71-Abstract-Conference.html) identifies exponential weighting as a source of false-negative sensitivity and proposes alternative pairwise activations. [RoDPO (2026 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.29259) reports that stochastic selection from a dynamic top-K pool outperforms deterministic hardest-negative selection in multimodal sequential recommendation. This supports testing controlled hardness, although its results do not establish gains for NextItNet. Sampling correction addresses a separate issue: [Correcting the LogQ Correction (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) accounts for positives being always included, rather than sampled; it does not identify latent positives.

For top-ranked discrimination, [SL@K (KDD 2025)](https://jiawei-chen.github.io/paper/KDD25-SLK.pdf) uses quantile-based truncation to target NDCG@K and includes sequential-recommendation experiments. Practical hypothesis for this task: retain one NextItNet scorer/category; score a bounded random candidate pool, exclude padding, targets and observed training positives, then mix uniform negatives with stochastically selected semi-hard negatives. Warm up before mining and cap hard-negative influence; these are proposed safeguards, not reliable false-negative identification. Compare multi-negative softmax against a robust PSL-style objective before adding quantile machinery. Training-history exclusions cannot remove unknown future positives, and full-catalog NDCG findings need not transfer to HR@10 over 100 candidates. Select exclusively through the pinned macro validation HR@10; larger training margins alone are insufficient evidence.
